summary: A pole lookout on the Flathead Indian Reservation near Jette Lake, dated 1935 or 1936 by sources that disagree; manned into 1960 and gone by 1969.

facts.design: 50-ft pole L-4 tower per firelookout.com; 1936 newspaper plans give four tamarack poles about 40 ft high, with the station on a platform
facts.status_note: firelookout.com gives Gone 1969; Forest Lookouts marks it Removed; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list reads Tower Gone.

events.note: firelookout.com's date for a 50-foot pole L-4 tower. Newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts place road and tower work in 1936.

Newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts: a crew began a right of way for a road about five miles long; the Indian Service received the new tower in October; work stopped in December until spring. Plans called for four tamarack poles about 40 ft high.
Fire weather readings began at the lookout (October 1957 item). The item does not name an observer.
A Daily Inter Lake item reports three brush and grass fires near Polson, at the lookout and at Rocky Point (August 1959).
Manned by Bill Dergelo that summer; closed for the year in September after late-summer rain lowered burning indexes (Flathead Courier).
firelookout.com: Gone 1969. No cause or method given.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. firelookout.com gives 1935 and a 50-ft pole tower; the 1936 newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts describe construction that fall and a station on poles about 40 ft high. The story reports both. The stored height_m of 12.2 follows the 40-ft figure.

notes_for_editor: Two independent web sources agree the tower is gone (firelookout.com: Gone 1969; FFLA list: Tower Gone) and that it was manned in 1960. Build date conflicts: firelookout.com says 1935, the 1936 newspaper items (cited through Forest Lookouts; originals from the Missoulian, Flathead Courier, Char-Koosta and Daily Inter Lake not checked) describe construction in 1936. Height conflicts: 50 ft (firelookout.com) versus about 40 ft (1936 plans). The 1956 NGS survey note reads like a station description, not a tower inspection, so it is not evidence of the tower's condition. Elevation 5,176 ft per firelookout.com; the record has no elevation field. Agency suggestion: the record's agency is null; the Forest Lookouts header and the 1936 items point to the Indian Service, Flathead Indian Agency. Searched once; the CSKT Fire Lookouts page is an interactive list and did not yield Jette text. No NRHP or site visit information found; the site's current condition and access are unknown.
